Parametric surfaces

Source: R/layers-parametric.R
stat_parametric_3d.Rd

Evaluates fun(u, v) on a regular (u, v) grid and triangulates it with indexed vertices, each grid quad split along its shorter diagonal. A closed direction joins its last row of quads back to the first samples by index, so a torus or a sphere has no seam; the end of a closed range is not sampled. A twisted closed direction reverses the other parameter across the seam, which closes a Moebius strip or a Klein bottle. Samples at coincident positions, such as the poles of a sphere, are welded into one vertex.

Usage

stat_parametric_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  fun,
  u = c(0, 2 * pi),
  v = c(0, 2 * pi),
  n = 40L,
  closed = FALSE,
  twist = FALSE,
  args = list(),
  adaptive = FALSE,
  tolerance = 0.002,
  angle = 10,
  max_depth = 4L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_parametric_3d(...)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

fun

Vectorised function of u and v returning x, y and z as a list, data frame or three-column matrix.

u, v

Parameter ranges.

n

Number of samples along u and v, scalar or two integers.

closed

Whether u and v wrap around, scalar or two logicals.

twist

Whether crossing the seam of a closed direction reverses the other parameter, scalar or two logicals.

args

Additional named arguments passed to fun.

adaptive

Whether to refine the grid where it deviates from fun.

tolerance

Midpoint deviation tolerance as a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal.

angle

Normal angle tolerance in degrees.

max_depth

Maximum number of refinement rounds.

Details

With adaptive = TRUE each edge whose midpoint on the surface lies further than tolerance times the bounding-box diagonal from the chord midpoint, or whose endpoint normals differ by more than angle degrees, is marked, and marked triangles are refined by conforming longest-edge bisection, up to max_depth rounds. Midpoints are shared by the triangles of an edge, so the refined surface has no cracks.

Vertex normals (nx, ny, nz) are the unit vector of r_u x r_v from central differences of fun; where r_u x r_v vanishes (poles) the area-weighted normal of the adjacent faces is used. Computed variables u, v, gaussian_curvature and mean_curvature (from the first and second fundamental forms, the mean curvature signed with respect to r_u x r_v) are averaged over each face, as is z_mean. Derivative stencils evaluate fun up to 1e-4 times the parameter range beyond the ends of an open range. Coordinates returned by fun are positions in the transformed scale space. Self-intersecting surfaces such as the Klein bottle are split where they cross by the visibility engine.

References

Rivara (1984). Algorithms for refining triangular grids suitable for adaptive and multigrid techniques. International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering 20, 745-756. doi:10.1002/nme.1620200412

Examples

torus <- function(u, v) list(x = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * cos(u),
  y = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * sin(u), z = 0.4 * sin(v))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_parametric_3d(fun = torus, n = c(36, 18), closed = TRUE) + coord_3d()
moebius <- function(u, v) list(x = (1 + v / 2 * cos(u / 2)) * cos(u),
  y = (1 + v / 2 * cos(u / 2)) * sin(u), z = v / 2 * sin(u / 2))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  stat_parametric_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = ggplot2::after_stat(u)), fun = moebius,
    v = c(-1, 1), n = c(48, 6), closed = c(u = TRUE, v = FALSE),
    twist = c(u = TRUE, v = FALSE)) + coord_3d()
